HEAVY IS THE CROWN — Site Code for AI Complete source and rebuild guide for the HEAVY IS THE CROWN static site. Live site: https://snowphamtom.github.io/hall-looks/ Source commit: 3959388060e2687324dd88617d82c3519309fc31 (hall-looks repo, commit “Point share tags at Pages and show the finish note on presets”) Contents: 68 files, 10,061,000 total: 27 text files and 41 images, in 12 HTML pages. Companion file: rebuild_heavy_is_the_crown.py (12,494,255 bytes (12201.4 KB), sha256 92725d4e603d9eeb03659216bca121f0e53a3e44d2bbf0d288ff23b4d6bad9bc) rebuilds every file byte for byte. Prepared: 2026-10-05 How to read this document Sections 1–6 explain the site: what each page is for, the file tree, how to rebuild and host it, how the code fits together, and the house rules. Section 7 lists the images with their sizes and sha256 hashes. Their bytes are not pasted here; they are embedded as base64 in rebuild_heavy_is_the_crown.py. Section 8 has the full source of every text file, one heading per path, in Consolas 8 pt. The one exception: forge/index.html carries six images inline as data: URIs (about 2.9 MB of base64). Those six base64 runs are replaced by a bracketed note giving their length and sha256. All other characters of that file are shown as they are. Appendix A has the text of rebuild_heavy_is_the_crown.py. To keep this document readable, every base64 run is replaced by a short note: the image payloads and the data: URIs inside forge/index.html. Use the companion .py file to rebuild; it has everything. 1. Overview HEAVY IS THE CROWN is a dark “hall of fighters” character site. The home page (the Room) says: “A dark hall of fighters. Open a look, build on the Forge, or keep what you save in the locker. The site background follows the highest rank you have saved; only Prism is holographic.” Five ready-made looks live in the hall: Foundation (the earned piece, rank 24 Prism), Black Chrome (rank 14 Royal), White Samurai (21 Ember), Skull Champion (8 Jade) and Titan Gladiator (11 Azure). Visitors can view each look in six styles, build figures on the Forge canvas, compose a character in Create, see weapons in Smith and fight pictures in the Colosseum, and keep up to 24 characters in one shared Locker. The Locker lives in the browser's localStorage. There are no accounts, no server code, no build step, and nothing leaves the browser. Pages (titles and descriptions are taken from each page's and meta description): The four fighter pages (Black Chrome, White Samurai, Skull Champion, Titan Gladiator) are “Look” pages. They share look.js: six style buttons (Realistic, Anime, 8-bit, Painterly, Ink, Clay) each show a separate picture made ahead of time, and an “Imagine prompt” box writes words only; it does not draw. Every page carries the same top navigation: Room, Foundation, Black Chrome, White Samurai, Skull Champion, Titan Gladiator, Forge, Smith, Colosseum, Create, Help, Locker. On narrow screens, nav.js folds the links behind a Menu button. 2. File tree with sizes Sizes are exact byte counts at commit 3959388. titan-gladiator/ index.html 4,295 white-samurai/ index.html 4,154 68 files, 10,061,000 bytes (12 directories) Note on the count: the site zip (heavy-is-the-crown-site-3959388.zip) lists 80 entries. These are the 68 files plus 12 directory entries (black-chrome/, colosseum/, create/, forge/, foundation/, help/, images/, locker/, skull-champion/, smith/, titan-gladiator/, white-samurai/). The git tree has 68 files. 3. How to rebuild Needs Python 3.6 or later and the standard library only. No network access, no pip installs. python3 rebuild_heavy_is_the_crown.py # writes ./heavy-is-the-crown/ and verifies it python3 rebuild_heavy_is_the_crown.py --serve # same, then serves it at http://localhost:8000/ python3 rebuild_heavy_is_the_crown.py --serve --port 9000 python3 rebuild_heavy_is_the_crown.py --out site # write to ./site instead python3 rebuild_heavy_is_the_crown.py --verify-only # only check an existing folder What the script does: Holds all 68 files. The 27 text files are raw triple-quoted Python strings (r"""...""") with the exact file text, so the code can be read in the .py file. The 41 images are base64, wrapped at 76 characters. Writes each file under the output folder at its original path. Text is written as UTF-8 bytes; nothing is re-encoded, re-indented or minified. Checks every written file against an embedded MANIFEST of path → (size, sha256) and prints a summary. It exits 0 when all match and 1 when any file is missing or different. With --serve, it then runs http.server (ThreadingHTTPServer) on port 8000, serving the output folder. Tested output (run in a fresh temp folder): Wrote 68 files to /tmp/.../heavy-is-the-crown Verified 68 of 68 files against the sha256 manifest (27 text, 41 binary, 10061000 bytes total; source commit 3959388060e2687324dd88617d82c3519309fc31). OK: every file is byte-identical to the original site. The rebuilt folder was also compared with diff -r against `git archive 3959388` and against the unzipped site zip; both showed no differences. 4. How to host it Any static file host works: GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel static, S3/CloudFront, Cloudflare Pages, nginx, or `python3 -m http.server`. There is no build step and no server code; upload the folder as it is. All links between pages, scripts, styles and images are relative (./ on the home page, ../ on subpages, and directory URLs like ../forge/ that resolve to index.html). So the site works at a domain root or under a subpath, as it does at /hall-looks/ on GitHub Pages. The host must serve a folder's index.html for a directory URL (for example /forge/ → /forge/index.html). Every common static host does this. .nojekyll is an empty file that tells GitHub Pages not to run Jekyll. Keep it for GitHub Pages; other hosts ignore it. Absolute URLs appear only in share tags: og:url, og:image and twitter:image point to https://snowphamtom.github.io/hall-looks/. Links and navigation do not depend on them. On a new domain, update them so link previews point at the new copy. The only external request is Google Fonts (Cormorant Garamond and Outfit from fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com). Without it the pages fall back to system fonts. Opening the files straight from disk (file://) mostly works, but serve them over http (for example with --serve) so directory links and localStorage behave like the live site. 5. Architecture Plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript: no framework, no bundler, no modules. Each page loads its scripts with ordinary <script src> tags in a fixed order, and the shared scripts publish small globals on window. 5.1 Which JS file drives what 5.2 CSS styles.css — the main site stylesheet: :root variables (--bg #070708, --ink #F4F1E8, amber, etc.), nav, layout, look pages, locker and the rank field (body[data-rank] tints and the holographic Prism field). Used by every page except Forge. card.css — the shared character card (“Gallery full-art”): .hc-grid and .hc-card with art, foil, sheen, rank emblem and name plate. Its header says “Only .hc-card--prism gets foil.” Used by Home, Locker, Create, Smith, Colosseum and Forge. create.css — extra rules for the Create page only (“CREATE-PART.css”); it builds on styles.css variables. forge/index.html — carries its own inline <style>. 5.3 Locker storage (localStorage) All locker data stays in the visitor's browser. Same keys on every page, including the Forge's own copy: Rank of a saved character (locker-field.js rankForCharacter): a saved look keeps its look's rank (Skull Champion 8, Titan Gladiator 11, Black Chrome 14, White Samurai 21, Foundation 24). A Forge save that starts from a look takes that look's rank. A blank Forge figure starts at Ashen (1) and moves up one rank per changed setting, up to Scarlet (23). Only Foundation reaches Prism (24). The page background takes the color of the single highest saved rank. 5.4 Images images/ holds: look-<look>-<style> (4 looks × 6 styles; realistic is .jpg, the others .png), fight-<a>-<b>.png (6 pairings), weapon-*.jpg (4), locker-*.webp (3 roster pictures), foundation.jpg, home-arbiter-plate.jpg (the home plate), king-schematic.jpg (the home page background, set in styles.css), and og-home.jpg (1200×630 share image). 6. House rules Three rules must hold in any change to this site: No currency anywhere. There are no prices, coins, balances or purchases in the code. The Help page states it as the first house rule: “There is no currency anywhere.” Trades in the game are barter only. Locker cap 24. CAPACITY = 24 in locker-store.js and in the Forge's inline locker. add() refuses a 25th save, and the UI reads “n / 24” and “Locker full (24)”. Only rank 24 gets the foil. Prism (rank 24, held by Foundation) is the one holographic rank. card.js adds .hc-card--prism only when rank === 24, card.css gives the foil only to .hc-card--prism, and locker-field.js turns the page field holographic only at Prism. Other ranks get a flat tint. The Help page also lists these house rules, quoted as written: There is no currency anywhere. Level shows only as armor wear. One crown war a day. The hall of champions is not a live ranking. It updates only when someone has a crown and a full locker of 24. The ultimate champion gets a custom crown and an iridescent, holographic locker character. Ranking is by originality, difficulty, creativeness, realistic application and rarity. Trades are barter only and need both sides to agree. They cover saved characters, weapons, armor, designs and techniques. Outside sellers get only the pay-to-play practice zone, with practice swords and commoner clothing. Help adds: “These are the rules of the game. This site does not run crown wars, trades, rankings or a practice zone yet; it has no accounts and nothing leaves your browser.” Other conventions in the code: pre-made pictures are labeled as made ahead of time, prompt boxes say they write words only, costume names (BeO, Ti-6Al-4V, Halbach) are not material claims, and labels are plain and literal. 7. Images The 41 images (6,873,672 bytes (6712.6 KB)) are embedded as base64 in rebuild_heavy_is_the_crown.py, not pasted as base64 here, so this document stays readable. Running the script writes them back byte for byte and checks each sha256. 7.1 Previews Small preview thumbnails (re-encoded, not the original bytes): the home plate and the four realistic looks. 7.2 Image list forge/index.html also carries six images inline as data: URIs. They are part of that text file (see section 8 for their lengths and hashes). 8. Full source of every text file Each file is shown exactly as committed (UTF-8, LF line endings), one line per paragraph, Consolas 8 pt. Tabs are kept as tabs. Long lines wrap on the page but are single lines in the file.     HEAVY IS THE CROWNRoomFoundationBlack ChromeWhite SamuraiSkull ChampionTitan GladiatorForgeSmithColosseumCreateHelpLocker
    

    
  
    A friendly field guide
    
  
    Help
    
  
    Start with a Look, build on the Forge, and keep your favorites in the Locker. Every control on this site does what its label says, right away.
    
  
    
    
    
      
    How do I say a character?
    
      
    Open Create and tap short names: ancestry (Elf is there), origin (Dark wood is there), then build, weapon, and a rank. A figure is drawn from your picks, and the page writes a markdown sheet. Say the line at the top, like elf, dark wood.
    
    
    
    
    
      
    How do I design a character?
    
      
      
        
    1. Open Forge.
      2. 
        
    2. Pick the left or right figure, then one of the four looks, or keep the blank figure.
      3. 
        
    3. Change helmet, chest, finish, color, weapon and the eight sliders.
      4. 
        
    4. Open Locker at the top and press Save to locker.
      5. 
      
    
    
    
    
    
      
    What are Looks?
    
      
    Looks are ready-made fighters: Foundation, Black Chrome, White Samurai, Skull Champion, and Titan Gladiator. On the four fighter pages, each style button shows a separate picture of that fighter, made ahead of time. The prompt box there writes words only; it does not draw.
    
    
    
    
    
      
    Forge sliders
    
      
      
        
    • Wear — how worn the armor looks.
      • 
        
    • Cracks — how many cracks show in the armor.
      • 
        
    • Armor glow — how bright the armor lights are (drawn on the blank figure).
      • 
        
    • Weapon length — how long the weapon is.
      • 
        
    • Battle damage — dents, burns and chips on the weapon.
      • 
        
    • Weapon glow — how bright the weapon glows.
      • 
        
    • Muscle — how heavy the build is.
      • 
        
    • Height — how tall the figure stands.
      • 
      
    
      
    The three weapon sliders and Armor glow draw on the blank figure. On one of the four looks they change the spec only.
    
    
    
    
    
      
    Forge buttons
    
      
      
        
    • Copy spec — copies the settings as text.
      • 
        
    • Save spec file — downloads the settings as a file.
      • 
        
    • Save picture — downloads a picture of the canvas.
      • 
        
    • Save to locker — keeps the character in your locker on this browser.
      • 
        
    • Load — puts a saved character on the selected figure.
      • 
        
    • Remove — deletes a saved character, after you confirm.
      • 
        
    • Keep today's crown — keeps today's crown for good. Then it reads Crown kept until tomorrow.
      • 
      
    
      
    Load and Remove only show next to a saved character.
    
    
    
    
    
      
    What is Locker?
    
      
    Locker is one locker for the whole site, kept in this browser on this device. It holds 24. Saves from Forge, Create, Foundation and the Locker roster all land there. The page background follows the highest saved rank, and only Prism (rank 24) is holographic.
    
    
    
    
    
      
    Smith and Colosseum
    
      
    Smith shows the weapon picture that goes with each look; your note shows beside it as words. Colosseum shows one fight picture for each pairing of two different looks, made ahead of time. No fight is simulated.
    
    
    
    
    
      
    House rules
    
      
      
        
    • There is no currency anywhere.
      • 
        
    • Level shows only as armor wear.
      • 
        
    • One crown war a day.
      • 
        
    • The hall of champions is not a live ranking. It updates only when someone has a crown and a full locker of 24.
      • 
        
    • The ultimate champion gets a custom crown and an iridescent, holographic locker character.
      • 
        
    • Ranking is by originality, difficulty, creativeness, realistic application and rarity.
      • 
        
    • Trades are barter only and need both sides to agree. They cover saved characters, weapons, armor, designs and techniques.
      • 
        
    • Outside sellers get only the pay-to-play practice zone, with practice swords and commoner clothing.
      • 
      
    
      
    These are the rules of the game. This site does not run crown wars, trades, rankings or a practice zone yet; it has no accounts and nothing leaves your browser.
    
    
    
    
    
      
    Common questions
    
      
      
        
    • Can I start over? Yes. Clear the Locker to remove its saved characters. Crowns stay.
      • 
        
    • Why did the background change? It takes the color of your single highest saved rank.
      • 
        
    • Why is only one rank shiny? Prism is the one holographic rank by design.
      • 
        
    • Will my locker follow me? No. It lives in this browser only.
      •

# path -> ("text", str) or ("base64", str); filled in by the data section below.
FILES = {}


def write_site(out_dir):
    written = 0
    for rel, (kind, payload) in FILES.items():
        if kind == "text":
            data = payload.encode("utf-8")
        elif kind == "base64":
            data = base64.b64decode(payload)
        else:
            raise ValueError("unknown kind %r for %s" % (kind, rel))
        dest = os.path.join(out_dir, *rel.split("/"))
        parent = os.path.dirname(dest)
        if parent:
            os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
        with open(dest, "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(data)
        written += 1
    return written


def verify_site(out_dir):
    ok, bad = 0, []
    for rel, (size, sha) in MANIFEST.items():
        path = os.path.join(out_dir, *rel.split("/"))
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as fh:
                data = fh.read()
        except OSError as exc:
            bad.append((rel, "missing (%s)" % exc.__class__.__name__))
            continue
        if len(data) != size:
            bad.append((rel, "size %d, expected %d" % (len(data), size)))
        elif hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != sha:
            bad.append((rel, "sha256 mismatch"))
        else:
            ok += 1
    return ok, bad


def serve(out_dir, port):
    import functools
    import http.server
    handler = functools.partial(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, directory=out_dir)
    httpd = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("", port), handler)
    print("Serving %s at http://localhost:%d/  (Ctrl+C to stop)" % (os.path.abspath(out_dir), port), flush=True)
    try:
        httpd.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\nStopped.")
    finally:
        httpd.server_close()


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Rebuild the HEAVY IS THE CROWN static site.")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=OUTPUT_DIR, help="output folder (default: ./%s)" % OUTPUT_DIR)
    ap.add_argument("--serve", action="store_true", help="after writing, serve the folder with http.server")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8000, help="port for --serve (default 8000)")
    ap.add_argument("--verify-only", action="store_true", help="do not write; only verify an existing folder")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if set(FILES) != set(MANIFEST):
        print("Internal error: embedded files and manifest disagree.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if not args.verify_only:
        n = write_site(args.out)
        print("Wrote %d files to %s" % (n, os.path.abspath(args.out)))
    ok, bad = verify_site(args.out)
    total_bytes = sum(s for s, _ in MANIFEST.values())
    n_text = sum(1 for k, _ in FILES.values() if k == "text")
    print("Verified %d of %d files against the sha256 manifest (%d text, %d binary, %d bytes total; source commit %s)."
          % (ok, len(MANIFEST), n_text, len(FILES) - n_text, total_bytes, SOURCE_COMMIT))
    for rel, why in bad:
        print("  MISMATCH %s: %s" % (rel, why))
    if bad:
        print("FAILED: %d file(s) did not match." % len(bad))
        return 1
    print("OK: every file is byte-identical to the original site.")
    if args.serve:
        serve(args.out, args.port)
    return 0

FILES['card.js'] = ("text", r"""// Shared character card: builds the markup and adds a light pointer tilt + sheen.
// Tilt is skipped when the visitor prefers reduced motion or has no fine pointer.
(function () {
  var reduce = window.matchMedia && matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
  var fine = window.matchMedia && matchMedia("(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)").matches;
  function el(tag, cls, text) { var n = document.createElement(tag); if (cls) n.className = cls; if (text != null) n.textContent = text; return n; }
  // o: {tag, href, img, alt, canvas, name, line, action, rank, rankName, tint, pos, size, contain}
  function make(o) {
    var card = el(o.tag || (o.href ? "a" : "button"), "hc-card" + (o.size === "sm" ? " hc-card--sm" : "") + (o.rank === 24 ? " hc-card--prism" : "") + (o.contain ? " hc-card--contain" : ""));
    if (card.tagName === "A") card.href = o.href; else card.type = "button";
    if (o.tint) card.style.setProperty("--tier", o.tint);
    if (o.pos) card.style.setProperty("--pos", o.pos);
    var art = el("span", "hc-card__art");
    if (o.canvas) art.appendChild(o.canvas);
    else if (o.img) { var im = el("img"); im.src = o.img; im.alt = o.alt || ""; im.decoding = "async"; art.appendChild(im); }
    card.appendChild(art);
    var foil = el("span", "hc-card__foil"); foil.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true"); card.appendChild(foil);
    var sheen = el("span", "hc-card__sheen"); sheen.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true"); card.appendChild(sheen);
    if (o.rank) {
      var r = el("span", "hc-card__rank");
      r.appendChild(el("b", null, String(o.rank)));
      r.appendChild(el("span", null, o.rankName || ""));
      card.appendChild(r);
    }
    var plate = el("span", "hc-card__plate");
    plate.appendChild(el("strong", null, o.name || ""));
    if (o.line) plate.appendChild(el("em", null, o.line));
    if (o.action) plate.appendChild(el("span", "hc-card__action", o.action));
    card.appendChild(plate);
    return card;
  }
  function onMove(e) {
    var card = e.target.closest && e.target.closest(".hc-card");
    if (!card) return;
    var b = card.getBoundingClientRect();
    var x = (e.clientX - b.left) / b.width, y = (e.clientY - b.top) / b.height;
    card.style.setProperty("--mx", (x * 100).toFixed(1) + "%");
    card.style.setProperty("--my", (y * 100).toFixed(1) + "%");
    if (!reduce && fine) {
      card.style.setProperty("--ry", ((x - 0.5) * 8).toFixed(2) + "deg");
      card.style.setProperty("--rx", ((0.5 - y) * 8).toFixed(2) + "deg");
    }
  }
  function onLeave(e) {
    var card = e.target.closest && e.target.closest(".hc-card");
    if (!card || (e.relatedTarget && card.contains(e.relatedTarget))) return;
    card.style.removeProperty("--rx"); card.style.removeProperty("--ry");
    card.style.removeProperty("--mx"); card.style.removeProperty("--my");

  document.addEventListener("keydown", function (e) {
    var t = e.target;
    if ((e.key === "Enter" || e.key === " ") && t.classList && t.classList.contains("hc-card") && t.getAttribute("role") === "button") {
      e.preventDefault();
      t.click();
    }
  });

  document.addEventListener("pointerout", onLeave, { passive: true });

})();

FILES['colosseum.js'] = ("text", r"""const stage = document.getElementById("stage");
const hero = document.getElementById("hero");
const empty = document.getElementById("empty");
const caption = document.getElementById("caption");
const status = document.getElementById("status");
const aBtns = [...document.querySelectorAll("#fighter-a [data-look]")];
const bBtns = [...document.querySelectorAll("#fighter-b [data-look]")];

const titles = {
  "black-chrome": "Black Chrome",
  "white-samurai": "White Samurai",
  "skull-champion": "Skull Champion",
  "titan-gladiator": "Titan Gladiator"
};

let fighterA = null;
let fighterB = null;

function front() {
  stage.classList.add("front");
  stage.scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" });
}

function setPressed(list, active) {
  list.forEach((btn) => {
    btn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", btn === active ? "true" : "false");
  });
}

function fightSrc(a, b) {
  const pair = [a, b].sort();
  return "../images/fight-" + pair[0] + "-" + pair[1] + ".png";
}

aBtns.forEach((btn) => {
  btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    if (window.heavyPulse) window.heavyPulse(10);
    fighterA = btn.dataset.look;
    setPressed(aBtns, btn);
    status.textContent = "";
  });
});

bBtns.forEach((btn) => {
  btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    if (window.heavyPulse) window.heavyPulse(10);
    fighterB = btn.dataset.look;
    setPressed(bBtns, btn);
    status.textContent = "";
  });
});

document.getElementById("start").addEventListener("click", () => {
  if (!fighterA || !fighterB) {
    status.textContent = "Pick Fighter A and Fighter B first.";
    return;
  }
  if (fighterA === fighterB) {
    status.textContent = "Same look on both sides. Pick two different fighters.";
    hero.hidden = true;
    hero.removeAttribute("src");
    caption.hidden = true;
    empty.hidden = false;
    empty.textContent = "Pick two different looks, then start the fight.";
    return;
  }

  if (window.heavyPulse) window.heavyPulse(16);
  const src = fightSrc(fighterA, fighterB);
  const line = titles[fighterA] + " vs " + titles[fighterB];
  status.textContent = "";
  caption.hidden = false;
  caption.textContent = line + ". One picture made ahead of time for this pairing; the fight is not simulated.";

  hero.onerror = () => {
    hero.hidden = true;
    empty.hidden = false;
    empty.textContent = "The picture for " + line + " did not load.";
    caption.hidden = true;
  };
  hero.onload = () => {
    hero.hidden = false;
    empty.hidden = true;
    front();
  };
  hero.alt = line;
  hero.src = src;
  front();
});
""")

HEAVY IS THE CROWN — Help























        HEAVY IS THE CROWNRoomFoundationBlack ChromeWhite SamuraiSkull ChampionTitan GladiatorForgeSmithColosseumCreateHelpLocker
        

        
  
        A friendly field guide
        
  
        Help
        
  
        Start with a Look, build on the Forge, and keep your favorites in the Locker. Every control on this site does what its label says, right away.
        
  
        
    
        
      
        How do I say a character?
        
      
        Open Create and tap short names: ancestry (Elf is there), origin (Dark wood is there), then build, weapon, and a rank. A figure is drawn from your picks, and the page writes a markdown sheet. Say the line at the top, like elf, dark wood.
        
    
        
    
        
      
        How do I design a character?
        
      
          
        
        1. Open Forge.
          2. 
        
        2. Pick the left or right figure, then one of the four looks, or keep the blank figure.
          3. 
        
        3. Change helmet, chest, finish, color, weapon and the eight sliders.
          4. 
        
        4. Open Locker at the top and press Save to locker.
          5. 
      
        
    
        
    
        
      
        What are Looks?
        
      
        Looks are ready-made fighters: Foundation, Black Chrome, White Samurai, Skull Champion, and Titan Gladiator. On the four fighter pages, each style button shows a separate picture of that fighter, made ahead of time. The prompt box there writes words only; it does not draw.
        
    
        
    
        
      
        Forge sliders
        
      
          
        
        • Wear — how worn the armor looks.
          • 
        
        • Cracks — how many cracks show in the armor.
          • 
        
        • Armor glow — how bright the armor lights are (drawn on the blank figure).
          • 
        
        • Weapon length — how long the weapon is.
          • 
        
        • Battle damage — dents, burns and chips on the weapon.
          • 
        
        • Weapon glow — how bright the weapon glows.
          • 
        
        • Muscle — how heavy the build is.
          • 
        
        • Height — how tall the figure stands.
          • 
      
        
      
        The three weapon sliders and Armor glow draw on the blank figure. On one of the four looks they change the spec only.
        
    
        
    
        
      
        Forge buttons
        
      
          
        
        • Copy spec — copies the settings as text.
          • 
        
        • Save spec file — downloads the settings as a file.
          • 
        
        • Save picture — downloads a picture of the canvas.
          • 
        
        • Save to locker — keeps the character in your locker on this browser.
          • 
        
        • Load — puts a saved character on the selected figure.
          • 
        
        • Remove — deletes a saved character, after you confirm.
          • 
        
        • Keep today's crown — keeps today's crown for good. Then it reads Crown kept until tomorrow.
          • 
      
        
      
        Load and Remove only show next to a saved character.
        
    
        
    
        
      
        What is Locker?
        
      
        Locker is one locker for the whole site, kept in this browser on this device. It holds 24. Saves from Forge, Create, Foundation and the Locker roster all land there. The page background follows the highest saved rank, and only Prism (rank 24) is holographic.
        
    
        
    
        
      
        Smith and Colosseum
        
      
        Smith shows the weapon picture that goes with each look; your note shows beside it as words. Colosseum shows one fight picture for each pairing of two different looks, made ahead of time. No fight is simulated.
        
    
        
    
        
      
        House rules
        
      
          
        
        • There is no currency anywhere.
          • 
        
        • Level shows only as armor wear.
          • 
        
        • One crown war a day.
          • 
        
        • The hall of champions is not a live ranking. It updates only when someone has a crown and a full locker of 24.
          • 
        
        • The ultimate champion gets a custom crown and an iridescent, holographic locker character.
          • 
        
        • Ranking is by originality, difficulty, creativeness, realistic application and rarity.
          • 
        
        • Trades are barter only and need both sides to agree. They cover saved characters, weapons, armor, designs and techniques.
          • 
        
        • Outside sellers get only the pay-to-play practice zone, with practice swords and commoner clothing.
          • 
      
        
      
        These are the rules of the game. This site does not run crown wars, trades, rankings or a practice zone yet; it has no accounts and nothing leaves your browser.
        
    
        
    
        
      
        Common questions
        
      
          
        
        • Can I start over? Yes. Clear the Locker to remove its saved characters. Crowns stay.
          • 
        
        • Why did the background change? It takes the color of your single highest saved rank.
          • 
        
        • Why is only one rank shiny? Prism is the one holographic rank by design.
          • 
        
        • Will my locker follow me? No. It lives in this browser only.
          •

  ];
  function blankState() {
    return { preset: null, desc: "", prompt: "", touched: false, helmet: "none", chest: "light", finish: "white", weapon: "katana", wear: 8, crack: 12, glow: 9, color: "#E8E8E8", wLen: 50, wWear: 40, wGlow: 8, mus: 50, height: 50, baseHelmet: "none", baseChest: "light", baseFinish: "white", baseColor: "#E8E8E8", baseWeapon: "katana", baseWear: 8, baseCrack: 12, baseGlow: 9, baseWLen: 50, baseWWear: 40, baseWGlow: 8, baseMus: 50, baseHeight: 50, basePrompt: "", baseDesc: "" };
  }
  function presetIndex(look) {
    for (var i = 0; i < PRESETS.length; i++) if (PRESETS[i].look === look) return i;
    return -1;
  }

    s.finish = s.baseFinish = p.finish;
    s.weapon = s.baseWeapon = p.weapon;

.rank-ladder {

  gap: 12px;
  margin: 6px 0 34px;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}
.rank-ladder li {

  position: absolute;

.rank-ladder .tier-apex { grid-column: 1 / -1; min-height: 132px; }

.rank-ladder .tier-apex { isolation: isolate; border-color: transparent; }
.rank-ladder .tier-apex::before {

  position: absolute;

  z-index: 0;

/* Help */
.help {
  max-width: 980px;
  padding: 56px 7vw 96px;
}
.help h1 {

.help-grid {

  gap: 16px;
}

  padding: 24px;

  font-weight: 500;

/* Immediate control feedback */
button { transition: transform .12s ease, border-color .12s ease, background-color .12s ease, box-shadow .12s ease; }
button:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(.985); }

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional, Tuple
import numpy as np

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AuditResult:
c12: bool
c60: bool
R_H: int
S_H: int
verdict: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CodecResult:
G_shape: Tuple[int, int]
HG_shape: Tuple[int, int]
full_shape: Tuple[int, int]
cond_clean: float
cond_dropped_mean: float

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class YetiResult:
domain_ok: bool
measure_val: float
defect_norm: float
positivity: bool
criterion_met: bool
gamma_yeti: float

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SealResult:
audit: AuditResult
codec: CodecResult
hall_prism: bool

 yeti: YetiResult
def __repr__(self) -> str:
return (
f"# -> audit c12={self.audit.c12}, c60={self.audit.c60}, "
f"R_H={self.audit.R_H}, S_H={self.audit.S_H}, verdict {self.audit.verdict}\n"
f"# -> codec G {self.codec.G_shape[0]}x{self.codec.G_shape[1]} + "
f"HG {self.codec.HG_shape[0]}x{self.codec.HG_shape[1]}, full {self.codec.full_shape[0]}, "
f"cond ~{self.codec.cond_dropped_mean:.1f} at 40 drops\n"
f"# -> hall prism={self.hall_prism} (coherence lock threshold >= 24)\n"
f"# -> yeti pipeline domain={self.yeti.domain_ok} / measure={self.yeti.measure_val:.4f} / "
f"defect={self.yeti.defect_norm:.2e} / positivity={self.yeti.positivity} / "
f"criterion={self.yeti.criterion_met}"
)

class CodeOfCodes:
"""
Executes a 54x8 tight frame codec, octahedral harmonic invariant audits,
critical-look Hall prism gates, and the 5-stage Yeti metric verification pipeline.
"""
def __init__(self, seed: Optional[int] = 42) -> None:
self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
self.n_modes: int = 8
self.mu: float = 54.0 / 8.0 # Tight frame factor: 6.75
self._build_algebraic_frames()
self._build_audit_projectors()
self._build_algebraic_generators()
def _build_algebraic_generators(self) -> None:
"""Constructs discrete cyclic group generators and canonical symplectic form."""
w12 = np.exp(2j * np.pi / 12.0)
w60 = np.exp(2j * np.pi / 60.0)
# Mode harmonic rotation operators
self×T12 = np.diag([w12 ** (k % 12) for k in range(self.n_modes)])

 self×T60 = np.diag([w60 ** (k % 60) for k in range(self.n_modes)])
# Canonical symplectic form on C^8 (4-position, 4-momentum split)
self.J = np.block([
[np.zeros((4, 4), dtype=np.complex128), np.eye(4, dtype=np.complex128)],
[-np.eye(4, dtype=np.complex128), np.zeros((4, 4), dtype=np.complex128)]
])
def _build_algebraic_frames(self) -> None:
"""Assembles the isotropic Hyper-Generator (HG) and Gram-matched base frame (G)."""
w12 = np.exp(2j * np.pi / 12.0)
# 1. Hyper-Generator HG (6 x 8): Octahedral isotropic closure block
HG = np×zeros((6, 8), dtype=np.complex128)
HG[0, 0] = 1.0; HG[0, 4] = w12**2
HG[1, 1] = 1.0; HG[1, 5] = w12**4
HG[2, 2] = 1.0; HG[2, 6] = w12**6
HG[3, 3] = 1.0; HG[3, 7] = w12**8
HG[4, 0] = 1.0 / np.sqrt(2.0); HG[4, 1] = w12 / np.sqrt(2.0)
HG[4, 4] = -1.0 / np.sqrt(2.0); HG[4, 5] = -(w12**5) / np.sqrt(2.0)
HG[5, 2] = (w12**3) / np.sqrt(2.0); HG[5, 3] = (w12**7) / np.sqrt(2.0)
HG[5, 6] = -(w12**7) / np.sqrt(2.0); HG[5, 7] = -(w12**11) / np.sqrt(2.0)
self.HG: np.ndarray = HG / np.sqrt(3.0)
# 2. Base Frame G (48 x 8): Orbit generator completing frame tightness
target_GG = self.mu * np.eye(8, dtype=np.complex128) - (self.HG.conj().T @ self.HG)
eigvals, eigvecs = np×linalg.eigh(target_GG)
eigvals = np.clip(eigvals, a_min=1e-14, a_max=None)
t = np×linspace(0, 2 × np×pi, 48, endpoint=False)
phase_matrix = np.exp(1j * np.outer(t, np.arange(8)))
envelope = np.exp(-0.4 * (np.arange(48) % 6))[:, None]
G_proto = phase_matrix * envelope
# Project prototype rows onto exact Gram target: G^H G = mu * I_8 - HG^H HG

 sqrt_target = eigvecs @ np.diag(np.sqrt(eigvals)) @ eigvecs.conj().T
U, _, _ = np.linalg.svd(G_proto, full_matrices=False)
self.G: np.ndarray = U @ sqrt_target
# Composite frame (54 x 8)
self.full_frame: np.ndarray = np.vstack([self.G, self.HG])
def _build_audit_projectors(self) -> None:
"""Precomputes harmonic invariant projectors and normalized frame operator."""
self.Pi_audit = np×zeros((8, 8), dtype=np.complex128)
self.Pi_audit[0, 0] = 1.0
self.Pi_audit[6, 6] = 1.0
S_full = self.full_frame.conj().T @ self.full_frame
self.Pi_codec = S_full / self.mu
def audit_invariants(self, m: np.ndarray, tol: float = 1e-6) -> AuditResult:
"""Audits cyclic group action invariance and harmonic/symplectic kernel ranks."""
norm_sq = float(np.vdot(m, m).real)
if norm_sq < 1e-14:
return AuditResult(False, False, 0, 0, "REJECT")
# Group closure orbit audit: T^n m == m
m_c12 = np.linalg.matrix_power(self.T12, 12) @ m
m_c60 = np.linalg.matrix_power(self.T60, 60) @ m
c12_check = bool(np×isclose(np×linalg×norm(m - m_c12), 0.0, atol=tol))
c60_check = bool(np×isclose(np×linalg×norm(m - m_c60), 0.0, atol=tol))
# Harmonic projector rank in invariant subspace
proj_m = self.Pi_audit @ m
R_H = 1 if np.linalg.norm(proj_m) > tol else 0
# Symplectic form pairing rank
omega_val = np.abs(np.vdot(m, self.J @ m))
S_H = 1 if omega_val >= 0.0 else 0
verdict = "ADMIT" if (c12_check and c60_check and R_H == 1 and S_H == 1) else "REJECT"
return AuditResult(c12_check, c60_check, R_H, S_H, verdict)

 def evaluate_codec(self, n_trials: int = 150, drops: int = 40) -> CodecResult:
"""Evaluates frame stability under clean and heavy row erasure conditions."""
cond_clean = float(np.linalg.cond(self.full_frame))
n_rows = self.full_frame.shape[0]
n_surviving = n_rows - drops
conds = np.empty(n_trials, dtype=np.float64)
for i in range(n_trials):
idx = self×rng×choice(n_rows, size=n_surviving, replace=False)
sub_frame = self.full_frame[idx, :]
conds[i] = np.linalg.cond(sub_frame)
return CodecResult(
G_shape=self.G.shape,
HG_shape=self×HG×shape,
full_shape=self.full_frame.shape,
cond_clean=cond_clean,
cond_dropped_mean=float(np×median(conds)),
)
def evaluate_hall_prism(self, looks: int) -> bool:
"""Coherence gate unlocking condition (critical look threshold >= 24)."""
return looks >= 24
def run_yeti_pipeline(self, m: np.ndarray, tol: float = 1e-6) -> YetiResult:
"""Executes the 5-stage Yeti metric verification pipeline."""
m_norm = np×linalg×norm(m)
domain_ok = bool(m×shape == (8,) and m_norm > 1e-12)
if not domain_ok:
return YetiResult(False, 0.0, np.inf, False, False, np.inf)
# 1. State density matrix
rho = np×outer(m, m×conj()) / (m_norm ** 2)
S_full = self.full_frame.conj().T @ self.full_frame
measure_val = float(np×real(np×trace(rho @ S_full)))

 # 2. Defect commutator
commutator = self×Pi_audit @ self.Pi_codec - self.Pi_codec @ self.Pi_audit
defect_norm = float(np.linalg.norm(commutator, ord="fro"))
# 3. Positivity under invariant projection
H_metric = self.Pi_audit @ S_full @ self.Pi_audit
eigvals = np×linalg.eigvalsh(H_metric)
positivity = bool(np×all(eigvals >= -tol))
# 4. Criterion
gamma_yeti = float(defect_norm / self.mu)
criterion_met = bool(gamma_yeti <= tol and positivity and domain_ok)
return YetiResult(
domain_ok=domain_ok,
measure_val=measure_val,
defect_norm=defect_norm,
positivity=positivity,
criterion_met=criterion_met,
gamma_yeti=gamma_yeti,
)
def run_full_seal(self, m: np.ndarray, looks: int = 24) -> SealResult:
"""Executes full invariant audit, erasure resistance, Hall prism lock, and Yeti check."""
audit_res = self.audit_invariants(m)
codec_res = self.evaluate_codec(n_trials=120, drops=40)
prism_state = self.evaluate_hall_prism(looks=looks)
yeti_res = self.run_yeti_pipeline(m)
return SealResult(
audit=audit_res,
codec=codec_res,
hall_prism=prism_state,
yeti=yeti_res,
)

 if __name__ == "__main__":
coc = CodeOfCodes(seed=42)
# Mode input vector exciting invariant harmonic modes [0] and [6]
m_test = np×zeros(8, dtype=np.complex128)
m_test[0] = 1.0 / np.sqrt(2.0)
m_test[6] = 1j / np.sqrt(2.0)
result = coc.run_full_seal(m_test, looks=24)
print(result)

# Polished plate

Same objects as the pasted codec. No new frame, no new word, no new parity law.

The argument is the exact section. The float section is a witness of rounding only.

## Field and parameter

\[
\varphi = \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}, \qquad
t = \varphi^{-1} = \varphi - 1 = \frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}.
\]

Working field of the braid and the determinant: \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})\). The frame scalar also uses \(\sqrt{2}\), so the round-trip lives in \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2},\sqrt{5})\).

## Objects

1. Frame. \(R\) is the \(48\times 8\) stack of six copies of \(\sqrt{2}\, I_8\).
2. Burau generators on coordinate space of dimension 48. Off the active pair, the generator is the identity.
3. Word \(w\) from the pasted builder: 60 positive letters and 2 inverse letters, length 62. Product order is the code order: each new letter is applied on the left, so the last letter is the leftmost factor.
4. Permutation \(\pi(i) = 13i \bmod 48\).
5. Parity \(H\in\{0,1\}^{19\times 48}\) as written: center row on columns \(0{:}6\), six rows of length 4, twelve rows of length 2. 54 ones.

No packing theorem is claimed for \(H\). It is the incidence matrix written in the script.

Encode:
\[
m \mapsto c_1 = Rm \mapsto c_2 = \rho(w)\, c_1 \mapsto c_3 = P_\pi c_2 \mapsto (c_3,\ Hc_3).
\]
Decode inverts the steps in reverse and synthesizes with \(\tfrac{1}{12} R^{\mathsf T}\).

## Lemma 1 (frame)

\[
R^{\mathsf T} R = 12\, I_8, \qquad \tfrac{1}{12} R^{\mathsf T} R = I_8.
\]

Each block contributes \((\sqrt{2})^2 I_8 = 2I_8\). Six blocks contribute \(12I_8\). Synthesis is division by that scalar.

## Lemma 2 (local inverse)

\[
\sigma = \begin{pmatrix} 1-t & t \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad
\sigma^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ t^{-1} & 1-t^{-1} \end{pmatrix}.
\]

For \(t\neq 0\),
\[
\sigma\sigma^{-1} = \sigma^{-1}\sigma = I_2,
\quad \det\sigma = -t,
\quad \det\sigma^{-1} = -t^{-1}.
\]

Entry expansion of \(\sigma\sigma^{-1}\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(1,1) &= t\cdot t^{-1} = 1,\\
(1,2) &= (1-t) + t(1-t^{-1}) = 1-t+t-1 = 0,\\
(2,1) &= 0,\\
(2,2) &= 1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Entry expansion of \(\sigma^{-1}\sigma\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(1,1) &= 1,\\
(1,2) &= 0,\\
(2,1) &= t^{-1}(1-t) + (1-t^{-1}) = t^{-1}-1+1-t^{-1} = 0,\\
(2,2) &= t^{-1}\cdot t = 1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Determinants: \(\det\sigma = (1-t)\cdot 0 - t\cdot 1 = -t\), and \(\det\sigma^{-1} = 0\cdot(1-t^{-1}) - 1\cdot t^{-1} = -t^{-1}\).

The \(48\times 48\) generator agrees with \(I_{48}\) off rows and columns \(\{i,i+1\}\). Conjugating by a coordinate permutation puts the active block in the leading \(2\times 2\) and \(I_{46}\) in the complement, so its determinant equals \(\det\) of the \(2\times 2\) block.

## Lemma 3 (word inverse and determinant)

Let \(\rho(w)\) be the product in code order, and let \(\rho_{\mathrm{inv}}(w)\) apply the opposite letter of each factor in reverse word order, also on the left. Then
\[
\rho(w)\,\rho_{\mathrm{inv}}(w) = \rho_{\mathrm{inv}}(w)\,\rho(w) = I_{48},
\]
\[
\det\rho(w) = t^{58} = \varphi^{-58}.
\]

Code order is left application: start at \(I_{48}\), and for each letter replace \(M\) by \(SM\). The last letter of \(w\) is the leftmost factor. Write \(w = (s_1,\ldots,s_L)\) and \(\rho(w) = s_L\cdots s_1\).

The inverse builder walks \(w\) backwards and applies the opposite letter on the left, so
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{inv}}(w) = s_1^{-1}\cdots s_L^{-1}.
\]
Induction on \(L\). The empty word gives \(I_{48}\) on both sides. If the identity holds for \(w\), the word \(w\) followed by one letter \(s\) has
\[
\rho(w{+}s) = s\,\rho(w), \qquad \rho_{\mathrm{inv}}(w{+}s) = \rho_{\mathrm{inv}}(w)\, s^{-1},
\]
and Lemma 2 gives \(s s^{-1} = s^{-1}s = I_{48}\). Both orders cancel. The written word has 60 positive letters and 2 inverse letters, so
\[
\det\rho(w) = (-t)^{60}(-t^{-1})^{2} = t^{58},
\]
the sign positive because both exponents are even. Since \(t=\varphi^{-1}\),
\[
t^{58} = \varphi^{-58} = F_{59} - F_{58}\,\varphi = \frac{(\sqrt{5}-1)^{58}}{2^{58}},
\]
with \(F_{58} = 591286729879\) and \(F_{59} = 956722026041\). The general form is \(\varphi^{-n} = (-1)^{n}(F_{n+1} - F_{n}\varphi)\); the sign is positive here because 58 is even. The integer expansion \((\sqrt{5}-1)^{58} = A + B\sqrt{5}\) has
\[
\begin{aligned}
A &= 190542951155155315760893526016,\\
B &= -85213398283269872748999999488.
\end{aligned}
\]

The decimal \(7.563396\times 10^{-13}\) is this value. Small determinant does not mean singular: the condition number of the float matrix is about \(2003\), and Lemma 3 already supplies the inverse.

## Lemma 4 (permutation)

\(\gcd(13,48)=1\) and \(13\cdot 37 = 481 = 10\cdot 48 + 1\), so \(\pi\) is a bijection and \(\pi^{-1}(j) = 37j \bmod 48\).

## Lemma 5 (clean syndrome)

Encode sets the tail equal to \(Hc_3\). The syndrome \(Hc_3 - p\) is the zero vector in \(\mathbb{R}^{19}\).

## Theorem (clean round-trip)

For every \(m\in\mathbb{R}^{8}\),
\[
\mathrm{decode}(\mathrm{encode}(m)) = m
\]
exactly, in \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2},\sqrt{5})\).

Encode applies \(R\), then \(\rho(w)\), then \(P_\pi\), then appends \(Hc_3\). Decode applies \(P_\pi^{-1}\), then \(\rho(w)^{-1}\), then \(\tfrac{1}{12} R^{\mathsf T}\), by Lemmas 4, 3, and 1. Each step is a two-sided inverse of the step it undoes.

## Theorem (detection is not correction)

\(H\) has rank 19 and nullity 29. It has 54 ones, 19 column-equality classes, and no singleton column.

| support rows | columns |
|---|---|
| \((0,1)\) | \(0,1,2,3\) |
| \((0,2)\) | \(4,5\) |
| \((2,)\) | \(6,7\) |
| \((3,)\) | \(8\)–\(11\) |
| \((4,)\) | \(12\)–\(15\) |
| \((5,)\) | \(16\)–\(19\) |
| \((6,)\) | \(20\)–\(23\) |
| \((7,)\) through \((18,)\) | twelve pairs, \(24\)–\(47\) |

Columns \(0{:}3\) meet the center row and row 1. Columns \(4{:}5\) meet the center row and row 2. Columns \(6{:}7\) meet only row 2. Each later length-4 row covers four columns and does not meet the center. Each length-2 row covers one pair. Equality of columns is equality of these supports. That is 19 classes and 0 singletons.

Rank, from the supports, without a rank call. Rows \(7\) through \(18\) have disjoint supports on columns \(24{:}47\), so they are independent, and they do not meet columns \(0{:}23\). Rows \(1\) through \(6\) are six disjoint 4-column blocks on columns \(0{:}23\), so they are independent of each other and of rows \(7{:}18\). Row \(0\) is not in that span. The only rows that meet columns \(0{:}5\) are rows \(1\) and \(2\). Matching row \(0\) on those columns forces both coefficients to be \(1\). Row \(2\) then equals \(1\) on columns \(6\) and \(7\), where row \(0\) is \(0\). Rows \(3{:}6\) and \(7{:}18\) do not meet columns \(0{:}7\). So row \(0\) is independent, and \(\mathrm{rank}\, H = 19\). The same count is the determinant of the \(19\times 19\) minor on one column from each class, columns \((0,4,6,8,12,16,20,24,26,\ldots,46)\): that minor has determinant \(-1\). Nullity is \(48-19 = 29\).

A payload spike of amplitude \(a\) at column \(j\) writes syndrome \(a\, H_{:,j}\). Every column in the class writes the same syndrome. The syndrome names the class and, when the fired entries agree, the amplitude. It does not name the column.

## Lemma 6 (payload versus tail)

These are two separate edits, not one combined edit.

Syndrome is \(Hc_3 - p\). A payload spike of amplitude \(a\) at column \(j\), tail untouched, writes \(a\, H_{:,j}\). A tail edit that decreases \(p\) by \(a\) on each row in the support of column \(j\), payload untouched, writes the same vector. Support does not say which of the two edits happened.

A combined edit does not cancel. On a weight-1 column supported on row \(r\), doing both adds \(a\, e_r\) from the payload and \(a\, e_r\) from the tail, and the syndrome is \(2a\, e_r\).

For the class \(\{4,5\}\) with support \((0,2)\), a payload spike of amplitude \(a\) at either column and a tail-only edit of amplitude \(a\) on rows 0 and 2 are the same syndrome.

## Lemma 7 (kernel)

The kernel of \(H\) is exactly the within-class differences. Columns in one class are equal, so \(H(e_u-e_v)=0\) whenever \(u\) and \(v\) are in the same class. The classes partition the 48 columns, so difference vectors from different classes have disjoint supports and are independent of each other. Inside a class \(c\) with representative \(c_0\), the \(|c|-1\) vectors \(e_{c_0}-e_j\) restrict to a star of rank \(|c|-1\). Their count is
\[
\sum_c(|c|-1) = 48 - 19 = 29,
\]
which equals the nullity. They are a basis of \(\ker H\).

A single spike is outside the kernel, so it is detected. An equal-and-opposite pair inside one class is in the kernel, so it is not detected. Syndrome zero does not mean the payload is the encoded payload.

## Corollary (a green syndrome is not recovery)

Take the clean codeword plus \(a\, e_5\) on the payload, \(a = 1/20\). The class is \(\{4,5\}\).

Subtracting \(a\) from column 5 returns the clean codeword, hence returns \(m\), by the round-trip theorem.

Subtracting \(a\) from column 4 also returns syndrome zero, because \(H_{:,4} = H_{:,5}\), and the leftover \(a(e_5-e_4)\) is a kernel vector by Lemma 7. The payload is then the true \(c_3\) plus that kernel vector. The synthesized vector is not \(m\).

Permutation direction. Encode sets \(c_3[i] = c_2[\pi(i)]\). Decode sets \(c_2[j] = c_3[\pi^{-1}(j)]\). A payload spike at index \(k\) therefore lands in the braid domain at \(\pi(k)\), not at \(\pi^{-1}(k)\).
\[
\pi(4) = 52 \equiv 4, \qquad \pi(5) = 65 \equiv 17 \pmod{48}.
\]
The inverse images \(\pi^{-1}(4)=4\) and \(\pi^{-1}(5)=41\) are the other direction and are not the landing.

The leftover \(a(e_5-e_4)\) in \(c_3\) is \(a(e_{17}-e_4)\) in the braid domain. The written word only uses generators \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_7\), so it mixes coordinates \(0{:}8\) and fixes coordinate \(17\). Applying the word inverse and folding the six frame blocks gives the message error
\[
\frac{a\sqrt{2}}{12}
\begin{pmatrix}
2(105+47\sqrt{5})\\
1\\
0\\
0\\
0\\
0\\
2(105+47\sqrt{5})\\
-(472+211\sqrt{5})
\end{pmatrix}
=
a\begin{pmatrix}
\sqrt{2}(105+47\sqrt{5})/6\\
\sqrt{2}/12\\
0\\
0\\
0\\
0\\
\sqrt{2}(105+47\sqrt{5})/6\\
-\sqrt{2}(472+211\sqrt{5})/12
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This vector is not zero in \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2},\sqrt{5})\). Its squared length at \(a=1\) is \(310975/36 + 34768\sqrt{5}/9\). At \(a=1/20\) the length is \(6.57198095964\), which is the float witness \(6.572\). The witness matches the vector. It is not the proof. The proof is \(H_{:,4}=H_{:,5}\) together with this nonzero image.

## Side identities, unused

These were checked and are not steps above.
\[
\frac{360}{\varphi^{2}} = 540 - 180\sqrt{5}, \qquad L_8 = \varphi^{8} + \psi^{8} = 47, \qquad S_0(1,1) = 1+1 = 2.
\]
At \(\lambda = 0\) the extra term in \(S_\lambda\) is zero. No other product is proved.

## Boundary

- A repair is valid only if the column is given.
- A zero syndrome after a guessed repair is not a recovery.
- Nothing here is a grant, a new invariant of the braid, or a statement about a physical constant.

## Certificate status

Exact checks that returned true: \(t=\varphi-1\); both block products equal \(I_2\) entry by entry; both block determinants; word count \(60+2\); \(\det = t^{58} = \varphi^{-58} = F_{59}-F_{58}\varphi\); integers \(A,B\); frame scalar \(12\); \(13\cdot 37\equiv 1\pmod{48}\); 54 ones; 19 classes; 0 singletons; columns 4 and 5 equal; columns \(0{:}3\) equal; rank 19 by the support argument; the \(19\times 19\) minor on one column from each class has determinant \(-1\); 29 independent within-class differences spanning the kernel; payload spike at column 5 equals the tail-only edit on rows \((0,2)\); the joint edit doubles that syndrome; braid landing \(\pi(4)=4\), \(\pi(5)=17\); sibling message error equal to the displayed vector, squared length \(310975/36 + 34768\sqrt{5}/9\); unused golden-angle and Lucas identities. Frozen inputs, read 2026-10-06 from intro-outro, not recomputed into new laws:

Codec radius stays one payload spike or one tail edit.

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from itertools import product

import numpy as np

PHI = (1 + 5**0.5) / 2
T = 1 / PHI
TOL = 1e-8

# Closed plate constants. Quoted, not derived here.
PHYSICAL_GRANT = False
MAGPIE = "19/658,750"
MEMBERS_GATE = "64/169,264"
BOOK_HEAD = 182
BOOK_PARENT = "259e15b770b7d2cc30a98638182ea2684ccd500271845f9ca5c34cbfcfd9da16"
COS_345 = 0.6
SIN_345 = 0.8
TWO_SIN_SQ = 2.56
TAN_THETA = 4 / 3


def beta(g):
    """Plate polynomial. beta(G) = 0.0104 G (48 - G). Not a branching proof."""
    return 0.0104 * g * (48 - g)


def members_headroom(required, interior):
    """H_i = I_i - C_i. Admit only if every required label matches and every H_i >= 0."""
    if len(required) != len(interior):
        return {"verdict": "REFUSE", "reason": "label length", "H": None}
    H = [i - c for i, c in zip(interior, required)]
    if any(h < 0 for h in H):
        return {"verdict": "REFUSE", "reason": "negative headroom", "H": H}
    return {"verdict": "ADMIT", "reason": "every H_i >= 0", "H": H}


def arbiter(interior, claimed):
    """interior - claimed. Missing HOLD. Negative REFUSE. Else GRANT."""
    if interior is None or claimed is None:
        return {"verdict": "HOLD", "delta": None}
    delta = interior - claimed
    if delta < 0:
        return {"verdict": "REFUSE", "delta": delta}
    return {"verdict": "GRANT", "delta": delta}


class PlateCodec:
    """Frame, Burau word, permutation, separating parity, plate gate.

    The 19x48 flower incidence is not the parity. Its columns were not unique.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.H = self._parity()
        self._certify_parity()
        self.word = self._word()
        self.rho = self._braid(self.word, inverse=False)
        self.rho_inv = self._braid(self.word, inverse=True)
        self.pi, self.pi_inv = self._permutation()
        self.R = np.vstack([math.sqrt(2) * np.eye(8) for _ in range(6)])
        self.plate = {
            "physical_grant": PHYSICAL_GRANT,
            "magpie": MAGPIE,
            "members_gate": MEMBERS_GATE,
            "book_head": BOOK_HEAD,
            "book_parent": BOOK_PARENT,
            "frame_is_E8": False,
            "rh_granted": False,
            "lambda_star_certified": False,
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _parity():
        cols = []
        for bits in product((0, 1), repeat=6):
            if sum(bits) >= 2:
                cols.append(bits)
            if len(cols) == 48:
                break
        return np.array(cols, dtype=float).T

    def _certify_parity(self):
        cols = [tuple(self.H[:, j].astype(int)) for j in range(48)]
        if len(set(cols)) != 48 or any(sum(c) < 2 for c in cols):
            raise RuntimeError("parity columns are not separating")
        if self.H.shape != (6, 48):
            raise RuntimeError("parity shape")

    @staticmethod
    def _word():
        w = []
        for _ in range(5):
            w.extend([(0, 1), (1, 1)])
        for _ in range(8):
            w.extend([(3, 1), (4, 1)])
        for _ in range(13):
            w.extend([(6, 1), (7, 1)])
        w.extend([(2, 1), (5, 1)])
        for i in (0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7):
            w.append((i, 1))
        w.extend([(5, -1), (2, -1)])
        return w

    def _block(self, i, inverse):
        M = np.eye(48)
        if not inverse:
            M[i, i] = 1 - T
            M[i, i + 1] = T
            M[i + 1, i] = 1
            M[i + 1, i + 1] = 0
        else:
            M[i, i] = 0
            M[i, i + 1] = 1
            M[i + 1, i] = 1 / T
            M[i + 1, i + 1] = 1 - 1 / T
        return M

    def _braid(self, word, inverse):
        M = np.eye(48)
        letters = reversed(word) if inverse else word
        for i, pw in letters:
            use_inv = (pw == 1) if inverse else (pw != 1)
            M = self._block(i, use_inv) @ M
        return M

    @staticmethod
    def _permutation():
        pi = [(i * 13) % 48 for i in range(48)]
        inv = [0] * 48
        for i, p in enumerate(pi):
            inv[p] = i
        return pi, inv

    def encode(self, m):
        c2 = self.rho @ (self.R @ np.asarray(m, dtype=float))
        c3 = np.array([c2[p] for p in self.pi])
        return np.concatenate([c3, self.H @ c3])

    def correct(self, received):
        received = np.asarray(received, dtype=float).copy()
        syndrome = self.H @ received[:48] - received[48:]
        if np.linalg.norm(syndrome) <= TOL:
            return received, {"status": "clean"}
        col_hits = self._match_column(syndrome)
        axis_hits = self._match_axis(syndrome)
        if len(col_hits) == 1 and not axis_hits:
            j, amp = col_hits[0]
            trial = received.copy()
            trial[j] -= amp
            if np.linalg.norm(self.H @ trial[:48] - trial[48:]) <= TOL:
                return trial, {"status": "repaired", "where": "payload", "index": j, "amplitude": amp}
            return received, {"status": "rollback", "where": "payload", "index": j}
        if len(axis_hits) == 1 and not col_hits:
            r, syn_r = axis_hits[0]
            trial = received.copy()
            trial[48 + r] += syn_r
            if np.linalg.norm(self.H @ trial[:48] - trial[48:]) <= TOL:
                return trial, {"status": "repaired", "where": "tail", "index": r, "amplitude": -syn_r}
            return received, {"status": "rollback", "where": "tail", "index": r}
        return received, {
            "status": "refuse",
            "column_hits": len(col_hits),
            "axis_hits": len(axis_hits),
        }

    def _match_column(self, syndrome):
        hits = []
        for j in range(48):
            col = self.H[:, j]
            support = np.where(col != 0)[0]
            outside = np.where(col == 0)[0]
            if np.any(np.abs(syndrome[support]) <= TOL):
                continue
            if np.any(np.abs(syndrome[outside]) > TOL):
                continue
            ratios = syndrome[support] / col[support]
            if np.max(np.abs(ratios - ratios[0])) <= TOL:
                hits.append((j, float(ratios[0])))
        return hits

    @staticmethod
    def _match_axis(syndrome):
        support = np.where(np.abs(syndrome) > TOL)[0]
        if len(support) != 1:
            return []
        r = int(support[0])
        return [(r, float(syndrome[r]))]

    def decode(self, word):
        c2 = np.array([word[self.pi_inv[j]] for j in range(48)])
        r1 = self.rho_inv @ c2
        m_hat = (1.0 / 12.0) * self.R.T @ r1
        frame = float(np.linalg.norm(r1 - self.R @ m_hat))
        return m_hat, frame

    def receive(self, received):
        """Correct if unique, then decode. Refuse does not invent a message."""
        fixed, info = self.correct(received)
        if info["status"] == "refuse" or info["status"] == "rollback":
            return None, info
        m_hat, frame = self.decode(fixed)
        info["frame"] = frame
        return m_hat, info

    def seal(self, interior, claimed, required, observed):
        """Plate gate. Codec success does not flip a closed refusal."""
        gate = members_headroom(required, observed)
        claim = arbiter(interior, claimed)
        return {
            "physical_grant": self.plate["physical_grant"],
            "magpie": self.plate["magpie"],
            "members_gate_receipt": self.plate["members_gate"],
            "members": gate,
            "arbiter": claim,
            "rh_granted": False,
            "lambda_star_certified": False,
            "frame_is_E8": False,
            "beta_48": beta(48),
        }


def _audit():
    codec = PlateCodec()
    m = np.array([1.0, 0.5, -0.3, 0.2, 0.1, -0.1, 0.4, 0.3])
    clean = codec.encode(m)
    got, info = codec.receive(clean)
    assert info["status"] == "clean"
    assert np.linalg.norm(got - m) < 1e-10

    for j in range(48):
        noisy = clean.copy()
        noisy[j] += 0.05
        got, info = codec.receive(noisy)
        assert info["status"] == "repaired" and info["index"] == j
        assert np.linalg.norm(got - m) < 1e-10
    for r in range(6):
        noisy = clean.copy()
        noisy[48 + r] += 0.07
        got, info = codec.receive(noisy)
        assert info["status"] == "repaired" and info["where"] == "tail"
        assert np.linalg.norm(got - m) < 1e-10

    double = clean.copy()
    double[3] += 0.05
    double[9] += 0.04
    got, info = codec.receive(double)
    assert got is None and info["status"] == "refuse"

    # Drive plate checks. These are the raw numbers, not a new derivation.
    assert abs(beta(47) - 0.4888) < 1e-12
    assert beta(48) == 0
    assert abs(beta(49) - -0.5096) < 1e-12
    assert abs(COS_345 - 3 / 5) < 1e-15
    assert abs(SIN_345 - 4 / 5) < 1e-15
    assert abs(TAN_THETA - 4 / 3) < 1e-15
    assert abs(TWO_SIN_SQ - 4 * SIN_345**2) < 1e-15

    # FIG. 2 from the start plate: C=[1,0,1,1], I=[1,1,0,1], refuse at label C.
    fig2 = members_headroom([1, 0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 0, 1])
    assert fig2["verdict"] == "REFUSE" and fig2["H"] == [0, 1, -1, 0]

    admit = members_headroom([1, 0, 1], [1, 1, 1])
    assert admit["verdict"] == "ADMIT" and admit["H"] == [0, 1, 0]

    assert arbiter(None, 1)["verdict"] == "HOLD"
    assert arbiter(1, 2)["verdict"] == "REFUSE"
    assert arbiter(2, 1)["verdict"] == "GRANT"

    seal = codec.seal(2, 1, [1, 0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 0, 1])
    assert seal["physical_grant"] is False
    assert seal["magpie"] == "19/658,750"
    assert seal["members"]["verdict"] == "REFUSE"
    assert seal["rh_granted"] is False
    assert seal["frame_is_E8"] is False
    assert seal["beta_48"] == 0

    gram = codec.R.T @ codec.R
    assert np.linalg.norm(gram - 12 * np.eye(8)) < 1e-12
    return {
        "clean_recon": float(np.linalg.norm(codec.decode(clean)[0] - m)),
        "payload": 48,
        "tail": 6,
        "double": info["status"],
        "beta_47": beta(47),
        "beta_48": beta(48),
        "beta_49": beta(49),
        "fig2": fig2["verdict"],
        "physical_grant": seal["physical_grant"],
        "magpie": seal["magpie"],
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    result = _audit()
    print("=== PLATE CODEC HYBRID ===")
    print("clean recon %.3e" % result["clean_recon"])
    print("payload repaired %d/48  tail repaired %d/6  double %s" % (
        result["payload"], result["tail"], result["double"]))
    print("beta(47)=%.4f beta(48)=%.1f beta(49)=%.4f" % (
        result["beta_47"], result["beta_48"], result["beta_49"]))
    print("FIG.2 %s" % result["fig2"])
    print("physical_grant %s  magpie %s" % (result["physical_grant"], result["magpie"]))
    print("frame is not E8; RH not granted; lambda* not certified")
    print("PASS")

48 message positions + 7 binary parity checks = 55-symbol codewords.

# Construction
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

N_MSG = 48
N_PAR = 7
N_CODE = N_MSG + N_PAR

def build_H():
    """Build the 7x48 parity-check matrix. Returns (H, masks)."""
    masks = [m for m in range(128) if (m & 1) and bin(m).count("1") >= 2][:48]
    H = np.array([[(m >> r) & 1 for m in masks] for r in range(N_PAR)], dtype=float)
    return H, masks

    v = np.asarray(v, dtype=float)
    if v.shape != (N_MSG,):
        raise ValueError(f"payload must have shape ({N_MSG},), got {v.shape}")
    t = H @ v
    return np.concatenate([v, t])

            d += f", column={self.column}, magnitude={self.magnitude:.6g}"
        if self.axis is not None:
            d += f", axis={self.axis}"
        return d + ")"


def _classify(s):
    """Core decision logic. Returns (kind, ...) tuple."""
    if np.linalg.norm(s) <= TOL:
        return (CLEAN,)
    sup = tuple(np.flatnonzero(np.abs(s) > TOL))
    col_hits = []
    for j in range(N_MSG):
        if sup == _COL_SUPPORTS[j]:
            vals = s[list(sup)]
            if np.all(np.abs(vals - vals[0]) <= TOL * max(1.0, abs(vals[0]))):
                col_hits.append((j, float(vals[0])))
    axis = [k for k in range(N_PAR) if sup == (k,)]
    if len(col_hits) == 1 and not axis:
        j, c = col_hits[0]
        if np.linalg.norm(s - c * H[:, j]) <= TOL * max(1.0, abs(c)):
            return (REPAIRED, j, c)
        return (REFUSED,)
    if len(axis) == 1 and not col_hits:
        return (TAIL_EDIT, axis[0])
    return (REFUSED,)


def decode(cw):
    """
    Decode a 55-vector codeword.

    Returns a DecodeResult:
      CLEAN     -> payload accepted as-is
      REPAIRED  -> single spike repaired; .column / .magnitude set;
                   syndrome verified to collapse after repair
      TAIL_EDIT -> parity-tail fault; .axis set; payload intact
      REFUSED   -> ambiguous or multi-fault; payload NOT trusted
    """
    vp, tp = split(cw)
    s = syndrome(vp, tp)
    r = _classify(s)
    if r[0] == CLEAN:
        return DecodeResult(CLEAN, vp)
    if r[0] == REPAIRED:
        _, j, c = r
        fixed = vp.copy()
        fixed[j] -= c
        # verify syndrome collapse before trusting the repair
        if np.linalg.norm(syndrome(fixed, tp)) <= TOL * max(1.0, abs(c)):
            return DecodeResult(REPAIRED, fixed, column=j, magnitude=c)
        return DecodeResult(REFUSED, vp)
    if r[0] == TAIL_EDIT:
        return DecodeResult(TAIL_EDIT, vp, axis=r[1])
    return DecodeResult(REFUSED, vp)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fault injection (testing / demonstration)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def inject_spike(v, j, e):
    """Return a copy of payload v with spike of magnitude e at column j."""
    w = np.asarray(v, dtype=float).copy()
    w[j] += e
    return w


def inject_tail(t, k, e):
    """Return a copy of tail t with edit of magnitude e at parity row k."""
    u = np.asarray(t, dtype=float).copy()
    u[k] += e
    return u


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Construction verification + full self-test battery
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def verify_construction():
    """Check the structural properties of H. Returns list of (name, ok)."""
    out = []
    out.append(("H is 7x48", H.shape == (7, 48)))
    cols = [tuple(H[:, j].astype(int)) for j in range(N_MSG)]
    out.append(("48 distinct columns", len(set(cols)) == 48))
    out.append(("min column weight >= 2", min(sum(c) for c in cols) >= 2))
    out.append(("common bit in every column", all(c[0] == 1 for c in cols)))
    bad = sum(1 for i in range(N_MSG) for j in range(i + 1, N_MSG)
              for k in range(N_MSG)
              if np.array_equal(H[:, i] + H[:, j], H[:, k]))
    out.append(("no pair-sum collision (1128 pairs)", bad == 0))
    return out


def run_selftest(seed=0, verbose=True):
    """
    Full functional battery. Returns True iff every check passes.
    Mirrors the proved fault model (a)-(d).
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    ok = True

    def rep(name, cond):
        nonlocal ok
        ok = ok and bool(cond)
        if verbose:
            print(f"[{'PASS' if cond else 'FAIL'}] {name}")

    for name, cond in verify_construction():
        rep("construction: " + name, cond)

    # (a) clean roundtrips
    errs = []
    for _ in range(5):
        v = rng.normal(size=N_MSG)
        r = decode(encode(v))
        errs.append(np.linalg.norm(r.payload - v))
        rep("clean roundtrip", r.status == CLEAN)
    rep(f"clean error ~1e-14 (max {max(errs):.2e})", max(errs) < 1e-12)

    # (a) all 48 single spikes repaired
    good = 0
    for j in range(N_MSG):
        v = rng.normal(size=N_MSG)
        e = rng.normal() * 10 or 1.0
        vp = inject_spike(v, j, e)
        r = decode(np.concatenate([vp, H @ v]))
        if r.status == REPAIRED and r.column == j and \
                np.linalg.norm(r.payload - v) < 1e-9 * max(1.0, abs(e)):
            good += 1
    rep(f"single spikes repaired {good}/48", good == 48)

    # (b) all 7 tail edits detected
    good = 0
    for k in range(N_PAR):
        v = rng.normal(size=N_MSG)
        t = inject_tail(H @ v, k, 3.7)
        r = decode(np.concatenate([v, t]))
        if r.status == TAIL_EDIT and r.axis == k and \
                np.linalg.norm(r.payload - v) < 1e-12:
            good += 1
    rep(f"tail edits detected {good}/7", good == 7)

    # (c) all 1128 equal-magnitude dual-spike pairs refused
    bad = 0
    for i in range(N_MSG):
        for j in range(i + 1, N_MSG):
            v = rng.normal(size=N_MSG)
            vp = inject_spike(inject_spike(v, i, 2.0), j, 2.0)
            r = decode(np.concatenate([vp, H @ v]))
            if r.status != REFUSED:
                bad += 1
    rep(f"equal-magnitude pairs refused, {bad} miscorrected", bad == 0)

    # (c) sampled unequal-magnitude pairs refused
    bad = 0
    for _ in range(200):
        i, j = rng.choice(N_MSG, 2, replace=False)
        v = rng.normal(size=N_MSG)
        vp = inject_spike(inject_spike(v, i, rng.normal() * 5),
                          j, rng.normal() * 5)
        r = decode(np.concatenate([vp, H @ v]))
        if r.status != REFUSED:
            bad += 1
    rep(f"unequal-magnitude pairs refused 200/200, {bad} miscorrected", bad == 0)

    # (d) sampled same-sign triples refused
    bad = 0
    for _ in range(200):
        js = rng.choice(N_MSG, 3, replace=False)
        v = rng.normal(size=N_MSG)
        vp = v.copy()
        for j in js:
            vp = inject_spike(vp, j, abs(rng.normal()) + 0.5)
        r = decode(np.concatenate([vp, H @ v]))
        if r.status != REFUSED:
            bad += 1
    rep(f"same-sign triples refused 200/200, {bad} miscorrected", bad == 0)

    if verbose:
        print("SELF-TEST:", "ALL PASS" if ok else "FAILURES PRESENT")
    return ok


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_selftest()

# codec55 — Complete [55,8] Fault-Refusing Codec

**Monsters Ink LLC · Docket MI-PPA-CODEC-2026 · October 6, 2026**

A complete, working error-correction codec: 48 message positions protected by
7 binary parity checks (55-symbol codewords). The decoder repairs isolated
single faults and **refuses** multi-fault events — never silently miscorrecting.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `codec55.py` | The complete codec library — construction, encode, decode, fault injection, self-test |
| `demo.py` | Walkthrough of all five behaviors |
| `H_matrix.csv` | The 7×48 parity-check matrix (also embedded in the library) |

## Quick start

```python
import codec55

payload = [0.5, -1.2, ...]          # 48 real values
codeword = codec55.encode(payload)  # 55-vector [payload; parity tail]

result = codec55.decode(codeword)
print(result.status)   # CLEAN | REPAIRED | TAIL_EDIT | REFUSED
print(result.payload)  # trusted payload (CLEAN / REPAIRED / TAIL_EDIT only)
```

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning | Payload trusted? |
|---|---|---|
| `CLEAN` | no fault | yes |
| `REPAIRED` | single spike located, repaired, syndrome verified collapsed | yes (`.column`, `.magnitude` set) |
| `TAIL_EDIT` | parity-tail fault; payload untouched | yes (`.axis` set) |
| `REFUSED` | ambiguous or multi-fault — decoder refused to guess | **no** |

## Proved fault model

- (a) every single payload spike (any nonzero magnitude) → repaired
- (b) every single tail edit → detected, payload intact
- (c) every dual spike at distinct columns (any magnitudes/signs) → refused
- (d) every same-sign multi-spike, order ≥ 2 → refused

Disclosed exception: adversarial mixed-sign faults of order ≥ 3 can alias
(outside the documented fault model). Seven rows are proved minimal —
no 6-row binary matrix can achieve these guarantees.

BACKGROUND
FIELD
This disclosure relates to error-correction coding, and more particularly to a real-valued block
code with a binary parity-check matrix that corrects isolated single faults while provably
refusing — rather than silently miscorrecting — multi-fault events.
DESCRIPTION OF RELATED ART
Conventional error-correction codes (e.g., Hamming codes, Reed-Solomon codes, LDPC
codes) are designed to correct up to a designed number of errors. When the number of errors
exceeds the code's correction radius, decoders typically either fail to decode or, worse,
miscorrect: they output a wrong codeword with no indication of failure. In safety-critical
systems — autonomous vehicles, spacecraft, industrial control, financial matching engines —

MI-PPA-CODEC-2026 — 1

 a silent miscorrection can be more dangerous than a detected failure, because downstream
logic acts on corrupted data with false confidence.
Some systems adopt a "rollback and refuse" posture: when the fault pattern cannot be
unambiguously resolved, the system refuses the operation and rolls back to a known-good
state. However, prior codes do not provide a provable guarantee that every multi-fault pattern
within a broad, practically relevant fault model will be refused rather than miscorrected. In
particular, for short binary parity matrices, certain pairs of faults can produce syndromes
identical to a single fault at another position ("aliasing"), causing silent miscorrection. What is
needed is a code construction in which aliasing is mathematically impossible across the entire
documented fault model, with a proof of minimality establishing that no smaller parity matrix
can achieve the same guarantee.

SUMMARY
Disclosed is a [55,8] real-valued block code defined by a 7×48 binary parity-check matrix H.
Forty-eight message positions are protected by seven parity checks, forming 55-symbol
codewords. The columns of H are the first 48 seven-bit binary masks, in lexicographic order,
that (i) have bit 0 set and (ii) have Hamming weight at least two — equivalently, the odd
masks 3, 5, 7, …, 97. Because every column contains the common bit (row 0), no two
columns are disjoint, and consequently no sum of two columns at distinct positions equals any
single column. The decoder computes a syndrome, matches it against single-column and
single-axis patterns, repairs only on a unique verified match, and otherwise refuses. It is
proved that: (a) every single payload fault of any nonzero magnitude is uniquely located and
repaired; (b) every single parity-tail fault is detected with payload intact; (c) every dual fault at
distinct positions, of arbitrary nonzero real magnitudes and signs, is refused; and (d) every
multi-fault of order two or greater with all magnitudes of the same strict sign is refused. It is
further proved that seven parity rows are minimal: no 6×48 binary matrix with the required
properties exists.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION
1. DEFINITIONS AND NOTATION
Let the payload be a real vector v ∈ R⁸⁸ (48 message positions). Let H ∈ {0,1}⁸×⁸⁸ be the
parity-check matrix defined in Section 2. The seven parity checks (the "tail") are t = Hv ∈
R⁷. The codeword is the 55-vector [v; t] ∈ R⁶⁶. On receipt of possibly corrupted values v′,
t′, the syndrome is s = Hv′ − t′ ∈ R⁷. A "spike" (payload fault) at column j with

magnitude e ≠ 0 contributes e·H_j to the syndrome, where H_j is column j of H. A "tail edit"
is a fault in one of the seven parity positions. The support of a vector, supp(s), is the set of
positions where it is nonzero.
2. CONSTRUCTION OF THE PARITY MATRIX
In one embodiment, the columns of H are generated as follows: enumerate the 7-bit binary
masks in lexicographic (numeric) order; select the first 48 masks that satisfy both (i) bit 0 is
set and (ii) Hamming weight is at least two. These are the odd masks 3, 5, 7, …, 97. The
resulting matrix is shown in FIG. 1 and tabulated in Appendix A.
This construction has three consequences, each verified by exhaustive machine check: (1) the
48 columns are distinct and each has weight at least two; (2) every column contains row 0
(the common bit), so every pair of columns intersects and no two columns are disjoint; (3)
there are no pair-sum collisions: there do not exist distinct indices i, j, k with H_i + H_j =
H_k (verified over all 1,128 column pairs). Property (3) is the structural fact that eliminates

aliasing across the documented fault model.
3. ENCODING
Given payload v ∈ R⁸⁸, compute t = Hv by binary-weighted summation (each tail position
sums the payload entries whose column has a 1 in that row). Output the codeword [v; t]. In
a software embodiment, H is stored as a 7×48 bit array and encoding is 48×7 multiply-add

MI-PPA-CODEC-2026 — 3

 operations. In a hardware embodiment (FPGA/ASIC), each of the seven tail positions is an
adder tree over the subset of payload lines indicated by the corresponding row of H.
4. SYNDROME COMPUTATION AND DECODER
On receipt of v′, t′, compute s = Hv′ − t′. The decoder proceeds as shown in FIG. 3:
• If s = 0: the codeword is clean; accept.
• Else, test whether s matches a single column exactly — i.e., supp(s) equals the support
of some column H_d and s is a uniform nonzero multiple of H_d. If exactly one column
matches, repair the spike at column d by the measured ratio, then verify syndrome
collapse (recompute the syndrome after repair and require it to be zero) before
accepting.
• Else, test whether s matches a single tail axis (a fault confined to one parity position). If
so, flag the tail edit; the payload is intact.
• Otherwise: refuse. Do not attempt repair. Signal the fault to the calling system (e.g.,
trigger rollback) rather than outputting a possibly corrupted payload.
The repair-or-refuse discipline is the central operating principle: the decoder never guesses. A
repair is performed only on a unique, verified single-fault match; every other nonzero
syndrome produces refusal.
5. PROVEN GUARANTEES
The following results are proved for the construction of Section 2. Formal proofs are retained
in the inventor's records.
(a) Single-payload correction. Every single spike at any of the 48 payload positions, of any
nonzero real magnitude, produces a syndrome whose support equals exactly the faulted
column's support with a uniform ratio, and no other column matches; the decoder therefore
uniquely locates and repairs it. Measured: 48/48 positions repaired.
(b) Single-tail separation. Every fault confined to a single parity-tail position produces a
syndrome on a single axis, distinguishable from any payload spike; the payload is accepted as
intact. Measured: 7/7 tail edits detected.

MI-PPA-CODEC-2026 — 4

 (c) Dual-fault refusal (complete). For any two spikes of arbitrary nonzero real magnitudes
and signs at distinct columns, the syndrome cannot match any single column: if the
magnitudes differ, the supports cannot align; if the magnitudes are equal, the common bit
(row 0) forces a non-uniform syndrome across the union of the two supports; if the
magnitudes are equal and opposite, the common bit cancels and the syndrome support lacks
row 0, which every column contains. Hence the decoder always refuses. Measured:
1,128/1,128 equal-magnitude pairs refused; 200/200 sampled unequal-magnitude pairs
refused.
(d) Same-sign multi-spike refusal. For any fault of order k ≥ 2 with all magnitudes of the
same strict sign at distinct columns, the syndrome cannot equal a single column: the common
bit forces the candidate ratio to equal the total sum, and same-sign summation then forces
every support position of the union to lie in every faulted column, contradicting distinctness of
the columns. Measured: 200/200 sampled same-sign triples refused.
6. MINIMALITY
Seven parity rows are minimal for the guarantees of Section 5. It is proved that no 6×48 binary
matrix with columns of weight at least two can be free of pair-sum collisions: eleven pairwisedisjoint triples of 6-bit masks are exhibited, each forming a collision of the form a + b = c
with a, b disjoint and of weight at least two, such that any collision-free set of columns must
delete at least one mask per triple — i.e., at least 11 deletions from the 57 eligible masks —
leaving at most 46 columns, fewer than the required 48. The 7-row construction of Section 2
achieves the guarantees, so seven is both necessary and sufficient.
